test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A civil servant is NOT allowed to become which of the following?

options.text: Private Secretary to Minister of the Union

solution:
The correct answer is __**Member of Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Member of Parliament (MP):**

 
 
• An elected representative in the Parliament of India.
 
• Representing the interests of their constituents in Parliament.
 
• Participating in debates and voting on legislation.
 
• Introducing and supporting bills.
 
• Overseeing the functioning of the government.
 
• Providing a voice for their constituents on various issues.
 
• Types: MPs can be members of either the Lok Sabha (lower house) or the Rajya Sabha (upper house).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Private Secretary to Minister of the Union:**

 
 
• A key aide to a Minister in the Government of India.
 
• Assisting the Minister in their official duties.
 
• Managing their schedule and appointments.
 
• Drafting official correspondence and speeches.
 
• Handling administrative tasks and coordinating with other government officials.
 
• Providing confidential and political advice to the Minister.
 
 
 
• **Cabinet Secretary:**
 
 
• The most senior civil servant in the Government of India.
 
• Head of the Civil Services of the Union.
 
• Advises the Prime Minister and the Cabinet on various matters.
 
• Coordinates the work of different ministries and departments.
 
• Ensures the effective implementation of government policies.
 
• Plays a crucial role in maintaining good governance and administrative efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Vice-Chancellor of a University:**
 
 
• The chief academic and administrative officer of a university.
 
• Providing academic and administrative leadership to the university.
 
• Maintaining the quality of teaching, research, and academic standards.
 
• Managing the university's budget and resources.
 
• Representing the university to the public and other institutions.
 
• Promoting the overall growth and development of the university.
